blockers.quote: A hundred backs. Facing the windows. And it's dark outside, so every window is a mirror. A hundred faces in the glass, all looking your way.
blockers.why: Check #11 Never say the feeling: this narrates exactly what line 402 already shows, weakening the visual discovery.
blockers.fix: Replace with: "He found the limit. You find the loophole."

blockers.quote: Now it's his news. Your turn to be the friend. Be honest: what number would open over your head? Tell us in the comments. And if you'd have done the same, hit like and subscribe.
blockers.why: Check #12 Leave fast: the first two sentences summarize the reversal, and the spoken subscription request drags past the cliffhanger.
blockers.fix: Replace with: "Be honest: what number opens over your head? Tell us in the comments."

suggestions.quote: Eleven. Home. The letter's already on the fridge, next to the jar where her paintbrushes have stood for six years. She's in the doorway, pulling on her vest. She doesn't turn round.
suggestions.fix: Make the transition causal: "But one face matters more than the hundred. Eleven. Home. The letter's already on the fridge. Your sister is in the doorway, pulling on her vest. She doesn't turn round."

suggestions.quote: Minus never proved they wanted you to fail. It only proved your win hurt. In one brain-scan study, envying a peer who did better at something that mattered came with activity in a region also active in pain (c05).
suggestions.fix: Cut the brain-scan sentence and move directly from "It only proved your win hurt" to the card's one-colour limitation, preserving the momentum of the notebook reveal.

keep.quote: Zero. Grey. One click. The biggest news of your life, and you're a receipt.
He isn't sawing your chair. He's building a ladder. Out of your mistakes. You've been his textbook for two years.
A face in a mirror is still a face. The toilets weren't broken. The one card you can't see was always yours.
